name: Florida
tagline: Two coasts, a ridge of citrus country, and the slow rivers in between.
intro: Florida's scenic highways follow A1A along the Atlantic dunes, US 1 down the long chain of the Keys, and the Gulf shore from the Panhandle to Sarasota, with inland roads under live oaks, through cattle country and along the St. Johns. This chapter follows the Florida Scenic Highways Program, run by the Florida Department of Transportation, and lists the national forest byway in the Apalachicola separately because it comes from a different program.

members.name: A1A Scenic and Historic Coastal Byway
members.blurb: Mostly two lanes for 72 miles, A1A threads the old Spanish streets of St. Augustine and runs on down the coast to Flagler Beach, ending at a seaside park named for a local folk hero.
members.note: Takes in the former A1A Ocean Shore Scenic Highway and A1A River to Sea Trail, which the national dataset still lists as separate roads.

members.name: Florida Keys Scenic Highway
members.blurb: US 1 crosses 43 keys on a long string of bridges, from Jewfish Creek down to Mile Marker 0 in Old Town Key West, and the designated corridor reaches five miles out into the water on either side.

members.name: Big Bend Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A two-day drive split between tall pine forest and the Gulf shore, from Tallahassee down to Apalachicola, with side roads out to the St. Marks lighthouse and St. George Island.

members.name: Florida Black Bear Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 40 runs through the sand pine of the Big Scrub, old dunes long since grown over, where Florida black bears live thicker than anywhere else and often keep close to the road.

members.name: Indian River Lagoon National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Two roads run down either side of the lagoon, US 1 on the mainland and A1A out on the barrier island, with causeways between them and the Kennedy Space Center a short way off.

members.name: Ormond Scenic Loop and Trail
members.blurb: A 34-mile double loop out of Ormond Beach, under tree canopy on Old Dixie Highway and back by the ocean on A1A, passing The Casements, where John D. Rockefeller spent his winters.

members.name: River of Lakes Heritage Corridor
members.blurb: The roads keep near the St. Johns, which the Timucua called the River of Lakes, between Sanford and DeLand, and pass Blue Spring, where manatees gather through the winter.

members.name: Scenic Highway 30A
members.blurb: A two-lane road along the Walton County shore, past rare coastal dune lakes and through Grayton Beach, a resort since 1913, and the white picket cottages of Seaside.

members.name: A1A Ocean Islands Trail
members.blurb: A1A leaves Fernandina Beach, a town that has flown eight flags, and runs south along the barrier islands, crossing the St. Johns River by ferry to the old fishing village of Mayport.
members.note: Route line from FDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Bradenton Beach Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Gulf Drive covers just under three miles of Anna Maria Island north from the Longboat Pass bridge, a beach road made for walking and biking, with boat ramps and picnic spots along the water.

members.name: Broward County A1A Scenic Highway
members.blurb: A1A follows the sand for 32 miles through Broward County's nine beach towns, from the Hillsboro Lighthouse in the north down past the Bonnet House in Fort Lauderdale, with sea turtle nests in the dunes.

members.name: Courtney Campbell Scenic Highway
members.blurb: SR 60 crosses Old Tampa Bay at sea level, past palms and mangroves, on a causeway a dredging man opened in 1934 under his own name, renamed in 1948 for a congressman.

members.name: Green Mountain Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Back roads rise and fall over the rolling hills near Lake Apopka, a favorite of cyclists, and pass through Winter Garden, where the West Orange Trail runs right down the middle of town.

members.name: Halifax Heritage Byway
members.blurb: Three loops around Daytona Beach and the Halifax River, by the hard-packed beach where cars still drive down to the waves, and south to Ponce Inlet, where the state's tallest lighthouse stands at the road's end.
members.note: Designated in 2020. FDOT has not published a route line for it yet, so it is listed here without one.

members.name: Heritage Crossroads: Miles of History Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Back roads around Bunnell that travelers have used for three centuries, among them the Old Brick Road, one of the state's first real highways, finished about 1917 and still open to bikes and cars.

members.name: Indian River Lagoon - Treasure Coast Scenic Highway
members.blurb: A1A on the dunes and US 1 on the mainland meet at Fort Pierce, with the mangrove banks of the Indian River Lagoon between them and Florida's first underwater archaeological preserve on the route.

members.name: J.C. Penney Memorial Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Three miles of SR 16 under old oaks and magnolias lead into Penney Farms, the town J.C. Penney founded in the 1920s, with the French Norman buildings of his retirement community and a bronze statue of the man.
members.note: Route line from FDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lemon Bay/Myakka Trail Scenic Highway
members.blurb: SR 776 runs between Venice and Port Charlotte through old Englewood on Dearborn Street, with turnoffs to the beaches of Manasota Key and the trails of the Myakka State Forest.

members.name: Martin Grade Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Twelve miles of CR 714 west of Stuart under an arch of hundred-year-old oaks, on a road that began as a logging trail and later carried cattle drives past citrus groves and ranches.
members.note: Route line from FDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Old Florida Heritage Highway
members.blurb: Country roads south of Gainesville wind past Paynes Prairie and through Micanopy to Cross Creek, where Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings wrote The Yearling in a cracker farmhouse, and sandhill cranes come down for the winter.

members.name: Palma Sola Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Manatee Avenue crosses Palma Sola Bay to Anna Maria Island on a causeway of picnic tables and fishing spots, named for a lone palm that sailors long steered by.

members.name: Pensacola Scenic Bluffs Highway
members.blurb: US 90 runs along the high clay bluffs above Escambia Bay, said to be the tallest ground on Florida's coast, past Bay Bluffs Park and the lone chimney of a Civil War-era mill at Red Bluff.

members.name: Scenic Sumter Heritage Byway
members.blurb: Country roads run through Sumter County's cattle and horse farms, down to cypress along the Withlacoochee and the shore of Lake Panasoffkee, in a county a 1925 magazine called the storehouse of Florida.
members.note: Route line from FDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Suncoast Scenic Parkway
members.blurb: SR 589 is a four-lane toll parkway running 42 miles north from Tampa into Hernando County, and the Suncoast Trail keeps it company the whole way through a long strip of greenway.

members.name: Tamiami Trail - Windows to the Gulf Coast Waters Scenic Highway
members.blurb: US 41 here is the old Tamiami Trail, opened in 1928, and for 70 miles it carries Gulf coast traffic from North Port up through Venice and Sarasota to the Hillsborough County line.

members.name: The Ridge Scenic Highway
members.blurb: SR 17 follows the Lake Wales Ridge for 39 miles from Frostproof up to Haines City, past lakes and citrus groves and through small historic towns like Babson Park and Dundee.

members.name: William Bartram Scenic and Historic Highway
members.blurb: SR 13 follows the east bank of the St. Johns south from Julington Creek under moss-hung oaks, along the river where the naturalist William Bartram once tried his hand at a plantation.

members.name: Apalachee Savannahs Scenic Byway
members.blurb: State roads cross the flat, wet savannahs of the Apalachicola National Forest, open grassland under scattered longleaf pine where pitcher plants and wild orchids bloom and red-cockaded woodpeckers live.
